decisions.reason: The source also constrains sensor-board connector placement, but that impact is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The surrounding context limits the bottom-side accessibility guidance to the vertically mounted main and sensor boards, not the power board.
This connector belongs to the power board, while the source guidance concerns the main and sensor boards.
The source changes mechanical placement policy but does not alter the sensor connector inventory, types, pinouts, or count; placement is already owned by the sensor-board mechanical Requirement.
The bottom-side placement policy does not change the interboard connector types, pinouts, power topology, or matching-order requirements.
Connector accessibility does not alter I2C pull-ups, series resistors, cable length, bus speed, or signal conditioning.
The general main-board connector placement constraint is represented by the source mechanical Requirement and does not change the panel power control's connector type, board, wiring, or behavior.
Mechanical connector placement does not affect the established ESP32-S3 GPIO assignments or compatibility policy.
The source does not change the BOOT control, reset wiring, or capacitance values; any connector placement constraint remains part of main-board mechanical layout.
The bottom-side connector policy does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module.
The source does not change USB-C programming or enumeration behavior; physical connector placement is governed by the main-board mechanical Requirement.
Connector accessibility does not alter the monitored rails, monitoring IC, channel allocation, measurement coverage, or monitor position.
